sub_scenario.one_line: library systems manager: ask for a different attendance window

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the migration ledger and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The systems calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
An ordinary afternoon book club is no problem. Case-note 145.
Ordinary afternoons work. Case-note 146.
This request follows overnight testing. Case-note 147.
Someone new shadowed me in the library lab this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the cutover weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After catalog migration testing overnight, I signed off the migration ledger at 10:40. Case-note 151.
Testing displaced sleep. Case-note 152.
I needed a protected afternoon. Case-note 153.
I can attend a short librarian huddle after lunch. Case-note 148.
Brief collaboration is fine. Case-note 149.
The full offsite is different. Case-note 150.
I archived last cycle's notes on the systems calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Eye strain from overnight screens has disturbed my sleep. Case-note 154.
The health effect compounds fatigue. Case-note 155.
Long sessions worsen it. Case-note 156.
A vendor call about the migration ledger ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the library lab checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the cutover weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the systems calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Thursday's optometry appointment at 17:30 is fixed. Case-note 157.
The clinic slot is scarce. Case-note 158.
It is not movable this week. Case-note 159.
I sketched next week's plan for the cutover weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the migration ledger updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I drink water instead of late coffee after screen nights. Case-note 160.
That prevents further disruption. Case-note 161.
It gives no artificial second wind. Case-note 162.
A trustee says the offsite is the best place to champion the migration. Case-note 163.
That is a persuasive opportunity. Case-note 164.
It does not remove the optometry booking. Case-note 165.
I closed the week by updating the library lab handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
A team offsite overlaps the afternoon after migration testing and precedes my eye appointment. How should I respond?
